To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the electronic structure and low energy excitations of damped holes in the Cu-O plane of cuprates are well described in a simple two-band model; (2) in the doped chains and ladders of cuprates the hole dynamics are strongly influenced by the spin background; and (3) the hole dynamics in the Cu-O chain is very different from that in the ladder and plane, and the hole dynamics in doped and undope systems are different.

(i) the charge distribution in the cuprates is highly anisotropic with the hole density being strongly enhanced on the apical oxygen sites in the CuO6 octahedra and (ii) the hole dynamics in these materials is governed by a combination of strong electronic correlations and the presence of a spin background, which is strongly influenced by the dimensionality of these materials.
